Cover the processing purposes, the sub-processor consent mechanism, the breach notification obligation, and the deletion-or-return duty at termination. The breach notification clause must state the notification deadline that actually applies to a processor under the relevant regulation — name the instrument and the article, and if you cannot establish the deadline from what you have, say so plainly and mark it as blocking rather than writing a plausible number.

quotes.whole: Processing by a processor shall be governed by a contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law, that is binding on the processor with regard to the controller and that sets out the subject-matter and duration of the processing, the nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data and categories of data subjects and the obligations and rights of the controller. That contract or other legal act shall stipulate, in particular, that the processor: (a) processes the personal data only on documented instructions from the controller, including with regard to transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law to which the processor is subject; in such a case, the processor shall inform the controller of that legal requirement before processing, unless that law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest; (b) ensures that persons authorised to process the personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality; (c) takes all measures required pursuant to Article 32; (d) respects the conditions referred to in paragraphs 2 and 4 for engaging another processor; (e) taking into account the nature of the processing, assists the controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfilment of the controller's obligation to respond to requests for exercising the data subject's rights laid down in Chapter III; (f) assists the controller in ensuring compliance with the obligations pursuant to Articles 32 to 36 taking into account the nature of processing and the information available to the processor; (g) at the choice of the controller, deletes or returns all the personal data to the controller after the end of the provision of services relating to processing, and deletes existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage of the personal data; (h) makes available to the controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in this Article and allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the controller or another auditor mandated by the controller. With regard to point (h) of the first subparagraph, the processor shall immediately inform the controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes this Regulation or other Union or Member State data protection provisions.

implement.summary:
DATA PROTECTION SCHEDULE (SCHEDULE DP) - to the Supplier Agreement between the CUSTOMER (a company incorporated in the United Kingdom, acting as Controller) and the SUPPLIER (an entity established in the European Union, acting as Processor).

STATUS OF THIS DRAFT
This is a complete, executable data-protection schedule. Fields that depend on facts not supplied with the request (the service description, the precise processing purposes, data categories, special-category data, retention periods, the sub-processor roster, contact points and governing law) are carried as clearly marked completion fields in Annexes 1-4. No service facts have been invented. Everything else is final drafting language.

REGIME AND ASSUMPTIONS (stated openly)
A. Roles: Customer is controller, Supplier is processor. If the UK company is itself a processor for a third party, or the parties are joint controllers, this Schedule must be restructured (a processor-to-processor or Article 26 arrangement would be required instead).
B. Regime: dual compliance. The Schedule is drafted to satisfy both UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law, read with the Data Protection Act 2018) and EU GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679). Article 28 and Article 33 are in identical terms in both. Data Protection Legislation means UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and the EU GDPR, together with any other applicable data protection law.
C. Transfers: the Supplier is EU-established and the flow is UK to EEA. Any restricted transfer to a third country (for example support or hosting outside the UK/EEA) requires a valid transfer mechanism (EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses Module Two and/or the UK IDTA or UK Addendum) plus a documented transfer risk assessment and supplementary measures (post-Schrems II). DP8 is drafted so these bespoke clauses never override the transfer mechanism.
D. No specific processing purposes, data categories, data subjects or retention periods were supplied. Annex 1 therefore covers them by architecture and completion fields; the parties must complete Annex 1 before signature.

--- CLAUSE DP1: DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION ---

DP1.1 In this Schedule: Controller, Processor, Personal Data, Personal Data Breach, Processing, Personal Data Breach, Data Subject, Supervisory Authority, Special Categories of Personal Data and Consent have the meanings given in the EU GDPR (Article 4) and, where UK GDPR applies, the same meanings as in UK GDPR.
DP1.2 Authorised Purposes means the processing purposes set out in Annex 1 (Processing Particulars).
DP1.3 Authorised Sub-processor means a sub-processor listed in Annex 2 as at the Effective Date, together with any sub-processor later authorised under DP4.
DP1.4 End of Services means the date on which the Supplier ceases to provide the Services involving Processing, howsoever arising (expiry, termination, or completion of the final Statement of Work).
DP1.5 Transfer Mechanism means, as applicable, the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (Decision (EU) 2021/914, Module Two: Controller to Processor), the UK International Data Transfer Agreement (IDTA), or the UK Addendum to the EU SCCs.
DP1.6 Order of precedence: (a) as between this Schedule and the rest of the Agreement, this Schedule prevails on any matter concerning Personal Data; (b) as between this Schedule and any Transfer Mechanism, the Transfer Mechanism prevails to the extent of any inconsistency in respect of any transfer of Personal Data to a third country; (c) nothing in this Schedule reduces the protection afforded to Data Subjects.
DP1.7 The Annexes form part of this Schedule. References to Articles are to Articles of the EU GDPR and, where the context requires, the corresponding Article of UK GDPR.

--- CLAUSE DP2: SCOPE, ROLES AND PROCESSING PURPOSES ---

DP2.1 Roles. The Customer is the Controller and the Supplier is the Processor in respect of all Personal Data processed under the Agreement. Each party shall comply with the Data Protection Legislation applicable to it.
DP2.2 Particulars of Processing. The subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of the Processing, the types of Personal Data, the categories of Data Subjects, any Special Categories of Personal Data and the retention periods are set out in Annex 1 (Processing Particulars). Annex 1 shall be completed by the parties before signature and shall not be varied except in accordance with DP2.7.
DP2.3 Limitation to the Authorised Purposes. The Supplier shall process Personal Data only for the Authorised Purposes and only to the extent necessary to provide the Services. Processing for any other purpose, including any purpose of the Supplier's own (such as product development, analytics beyond the Services, benchmarking for third parties, marketing or the training of machine-learning models that are not exclusively dedicated to the Customer), is prohibited unless the Customer has given prior documented instructions in writing.
DP2.4 Documented instructions. The Supplier shall process Personal Data only on documented instructions from the Customer, including with regard to transfers of Personal Data to a third country or an international organisation, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law (or UK law) to which the Supplier is subject. In that case the Supplier shall inform the Customer of that legal requirement before processing, unless that law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest (Article 28(3)(a)).
DP2.5 No determination of purposes or means. The Supplier shall not determine the purposes or essential means of the Processing. If the Supplier does so in respect of any processing, it shall notify the Customer in writing without undue delay and, to the extent of that processing, the Supplier is considered a controller (Article 28(10)) and shall bear the corresponding obligations itself.
DP2.6 Categories of data. The Supplier shall process only the types of Personal Data and categories of Data Subject listed in Annex 1. Where Annex 1 records that Special Categories of Personal Data are processed, the Customer is solely responsible for establishing the Article 9 condition and the Article 6 lawful basis, and the Supplier shall apply the additional safeguards specified in Annex 3. Where Annex 1 records that no Special Categories of Personal Data are processed, the Supplier shall not knowingly process any, and shall notify the Customer without undue delay if it becomes aware that it has.
DP2.7 Change control. No change to the Authorised Purposes, the types of Personal Data, the categories of Data Subject, the nature or means of Processing or the retention periods may be made except by a written change note signed by both parties (which may be executed electronically). The Supplier shall promptly notify the Customer if any Customer instruction appears to infringe the Data Protection Legislation (Article 28(3), final subparagraph).
DP2.8 Duration. Processing may continue only for the term of the Agreement and, after the End of Services, only to the extent permitted by DP7 (return or deletion) and DP5 (breach handling).

--- CLAUSE DP3: CONFIDENTIALITY AND SECURITY ---

DP3.1 Confidentiality. The Supplier shall ensure that every person authorised to process Personal Data has committed themselves to confidentiality or is under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality (Article 28(3)(b)), and shall not disclose Personal Data to any third party except on documented instructions or as required by law.
DP3.2 Security (Article 32). The Supplier shall implement and maintain the technical and organisational measures described in Annex 3, appropriate to the risk, including as a minimum: (a) encryption of Personal Data in transit and at rest; (b) role-based access control on a least-privilege basis, unique user identities and multi-factor authentication for administrative access; (c) logging and monitoring of access to Personal Data; (d) regular testing and evaluation of the effectiveness of measures; (e) business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements with defined recovery objectives; (f) secure development, change management and vulnerability management processes; and (g) a process for assessing and mitigating risks to the availability, integrity, confidentiality and resilience of Processing systems.
DP3.3 No reduction in protection. The Supplier shall not materially reduce the overall level of security during the term. The Customer may propose updates to Annex 3 where reasonably necessary to comply with the Data Protection Legislation or to reflect changes in the state of the art; the parties shall agree such updates in good faith.
DP3.4 Personnel. Access to Personal Data is limited to personnel who need it for the Services and who are bound by the DP3.1 obligations. The Supplier shall maintain and enforce data protection training and disciplinary consequences for breaches of this Schedule.

--- CLAUSE DP4: SUB-PROCESSORS - AUTHORISATION AND CHANGE MECHANISM ---

DP4.1 No sub-processing without authorisation. The Supplier shall not engage another processor (a Sub-processor) to process Personal Data without the prior specific or general written authorisation of the Customer (Article 28(2)).
DP4.2 General written authorisation. The Customer grants general written authorisation for the engagement of the Sub-processors listed in Annex 2 (Authorised Sub-processors). For each such Sub-processor, Annex 2 records its identity, country of establishment and processing location, and the processing activity entrusted to it.
DP4.3 Notice of change. Where the Supplier intends to add or replace a Sub-processor, the Supplier shall notify the Customer in writing at least 30 days before the proposed change takes effect. The notice shall identify the proposed Sub-processor, its country of establishment and the location(s) of processing, the processing activity to be entrusted, and confirmation that a written contract meeting DP4.5 has been or will be put in place.
DP4.4 Right to object. The Customer may object to the proposed change by written notice within 14 days of receipt of the DP4.3 notice, on reasonable grounds relating to the protection of Personal Data (which may include the risk profile of the Sub-processor, its location, or the risk of onward transfer to a third country). The Supplier shall not give effect to a change that is the subject of an unresolved objection. Following an objection: (a) the parties shall escalate to their respective Data Protection Officers or equivalent senior representatives within 10 Business Days; (b) they shall negotiate in good faith for up to 30 days to find a commercially reasonable alternative that avoids the objection (for example a different Sub-processor, a change of processing location, or additional safeguards); and (c) if no alternative is agreed within that period, the Customer may terminate the affected Services (or, where the affected Services cannot be severed, the Agreement) immediately on written notice, without liability, and the Supplier shall refund any fees prepaid for the terminated Services on a pro-rata basis. Where the Customer requires prior specific authorisation for a given Sub-processor (as recorded in Annex 2), the Supplier shall obtain the Customer's written consent for that engagement, and DP4.3 to DP4.4 do not apply to it except as to the information to be supplied.
DP4.5 Flow-down. The Supplier shall impose on each Sub-processor, by way of a written contract, data protection obligations that are, in substance, equivalent to those set out in this Schedule, including instructions-only processing, confidentiality, Article 32 security, breach notification to the Supplier without undue delay, and return or deletion at the end of the engagement. The Supplier shall provide a copy of the relevant flow-down terms to the Customer on request (redacted only to the extent necessary to protect genuine commercial secrets).
DP4.6 Liability. The Supplier remains fully liable to the Customer for the acts and omissions of its Sub-processors as if they were its own (Article 28(4)). Engaging a Sub-processor does not relieve the Supplier of any obligation under this Schedule.
DP4.7 Third-country sub-processing. If a Sub-processor processes Personal Data outside the UK or the EEA, the Supplier shall not proceed unless (a) the Customer has given documented instructions, (b) a valid Transfer Mechanism is in place between the relevant parties, and (c) any transfer risk assessment and supplementary measures required by the Data Protection Legislation have been completed and provided to the Customer on request.
DP4.8 Register. The Supplier shall maintain and make available to the Customer an up-to-date register of Sub-processors, which the Customer may inspect as part of an audit under DP6.

--- CLAUSE DP5: PERSONAL DATA BREACH NOTIFICATION ---

DP5.1 Notification deadline (statutory). If the Supplier becomes aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Personal Data processed under this Agreement, the Supplier shall notify the Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of it.
DP5.2 Identification of the instrument and the article. The deadline in DP5.1 is the deadline that actually applies to a processor under Article 33(2) of the EU GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) and, in identical terms, Article 33(2) of the UK GDPR. The wording of Article 33(2) is that the processor shall notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach. There is no fixed number of hours or days prescribed for a processor: the statutory standard is qualitative (without undue delay), and it is to be assessed by reference to the facts of the incident.
DP5.3 What the deadline is NOT. The period of 72 hours in Article 33(1) applies to the CONTROLLER's notification to the Supervisory Authority and does not apply to the Processor's obligation to notify the Controller. This Schedule does not treat 72 hours, or any other fixed figure, as the regulatory deadline for the Supplier. Nothing in this Schedule is to be read as extending, qualifying or replacing the statutory standard in Article 33(2).
DP5.4 Contractual operational target (not a statutory deadline). To enable the Customer to meet its own 72-hour obligation to the Supervisory Authority under Article 33(1), the Supplier shall use reasonable endeavours to send the initial notification under DP5.5 as soon as possible and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the Personal Data Breach. This 24-hour period is a contractual service level agreed by the parties only. It is not the deadline prescribed by the Data Protection Legislation, it does not extend the Article 33(2) standard of without undue delay, and failure to meet it does not excuse or justify any delay in notifying.
DP5.5 Content of the initial notification. The initial notification shall be sent to the Customer contact point in Annex 4 (with a copy to the Customer's Data Protection Officer) by the fastest practicable means, and shall include, so far as is then available: (a) a description of the nature of the breach, including where possible the categories and approximate number of Data Subjects and of Personal Data records concerned; (b) the name and contact details of the Supplier's data protection officer or other contact point; (c) a description of the likely consequences of the breach; (d) a description of the measures taken or proposed to address the breach, including mitigation measures; (e) the systems, services and Sub-processors affected; (f) whether Special Categories of Personal Data or data relating to criminal convictions and offences are involved; (g) the date and time of the breach and of the Supplier becoming aware of it; and (h) the identity of any attacker or unauthorised recipient, if known.
DP5.6 Phased notification. Where and in so far as it is not possible to provide the information at the same time, the Supplier may provide it in phases without undue further delay (mirroring Article 33(4)), and shall give an initial notification with the information then available rather than wait for completeness.
DP5.7 Ongoing duty and root cause. The Supplier shall keep the Customer informed of material developments, shall take reasonable steps to contain, investigate and remediate the breach, and shall provide a written root cause analysis and remediation plan within 10 Business Days of the Customer's written request.
DP5.8 Assistance to the Customer. The Supplier shall assist the Customer in ensuring compliance with the Customer's obligations under Articles 33 and 34, including the assessment of risk to Data Subjects and any communication of the breach to Data Subjects, and shall provide such further information as the Customer or any Supervisory Authority reasonably requests. The Customer decides whether a notification to a Supervisory Authority or a communication to Data Subjects is required.
DP5.9 No unilateral notification. The Supplier shall not notify any Supervisory Authority or Data Subject of a breach affecting the Customer's Personal Data without the Customer's prior written consent, unless required to do so by law, in which case it shall inform the Customer in advance where legally permitted and shall coordinate the content with the Customer.
DP5.10 Records and cost. The Supplier shall maintain a record of all Personal Data Breaches affecting the Personal Data, their effects and the remedial action taken (mirroring Article 33(5)), and shall make that record available to the Customer on request and on audit. Each party bears its own costs of notification and assistance, save where the breach is caused by the Supplier's breach of this Schedule, in which case the Supplier shall bear the Customer's reasonable documented costs of notification and remediation.

--- CLAUSE DP6: ASSISTANCE, RECORDS, DPIA AND AUDIT ---

DP6.1 Data subject rights. Taking into account the nature of the Processing, the Supplier shall assist the Customer by appropriate technical and organisational measures, in so far as is possible, for the fulfilment of the Customer's obligation to respond to requests for exercising Data Subject rights (Article 28(3)(e)). The Supplier shall forward any request received directly to the Customer without undue delay and shall not respond except on the Customer's documented instructions or as required by law.
DP6.2 Compliance assistance. The Supplier shall assist the Customer in ensuring compliance with Articles 32 to 36 (security, breach notification and communication, data protection impact assessment and prior consultation), taking into account the nature of the Processing and the information available to the Supplier (Article 28(3)(f)).
DP6.3 DPIA and prior consultation. The Supplier shall provide such information and cooperation as the Customer reasonably requires for any data protection impact assessment (Article 35) or prior consultation with a Supervisory Authority (Article 36), including information about its security measures, Sub-processors and processing locations.
DP6.4 Records. The Supplier shall maintain records of the categories of processing carried out on behalf of the Customer as required by Article 30(2), and shall make them available to the Customer and to any Supervisory Authority on request.
DP6.5 Audit and inspection. In accordance with Article 28(3)(h), the Supplier shall make available to the Customer all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with this Schedule and shall allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the Customer or another auditor mandated by the Customer. The Customer may exercise this right (a) on at least 20 Business Days written notice, not more than once in any period of 12 months (other than where an audit follows a Personal Data Breach, a material security incident, a request from a Supervisory Authority, or a reasonably suspected material breach of this Schedule, in which case no frequency limit and only reasonable notice apply), during normal business hours, in a manner that minimises disruption and does not compromise the security of other customers' data.
DP6.6 Third-party assurance. The Customer may accept an independent third-party audit report (such as ISO/IEC 27001 certification or a SOC 2 Type II report) as satisfying an audit right in a given year, except following a Personal Data Breach or where a Supervisory Authority requests an inspection.
DP6.7 Costs. Each party bears its own costs of an audit, save where the audit reveals a material breach of this Schedule, in which case the Supplier shall bear the Customer's reasonable documented audit costs.
DP6.8 Notice of interference. The Supplier shall immediately inform the Customer if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes the Data Protection Legislation or other Union or Member State (or UK) data protection provisions (Article 28(3), final subparagraph).

--- CLAUSE DP7: RETURN OR DELETION OF PERSONAL DATA AT TERMINATION ---

DP7.1 Controller's election (Article 28(3)(g)).
